source.title: An Exponential Learning Rate Schedule for Deep Learning

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training results and a toy analysis bearing on training outcomes, but it studies an exponential learning-rate schedule and BN/weight-decay interaction rather than the claim versions' main interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training schedule comparisons and a toy binary-classification nonconvergence result. It does not test the listed versions' main claims about random-label memorization, width and spurious minima, depth and shortcuts, initialization, stability thresholds, or BN's accuracy-speed benefit. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study establishes learning-rate schedule equivalences and analyzes a toy BN–weight-decay interaction. It does not measure any version's specified effect: benchmark CNN training-error attainment, width-dependent local minima, depth degradation, initialization benefits, recovery above a stability threshold, or BN's comparative training speed and learning-rate tolerance. Its use of normalization's scale invariance does not establish those effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove schedule equivalence under scale invariance, including weight decay and momentum, and verify related behavior on PreResNet32/CIFAR-10. Their toy analysis shows convergence with BN or weight decay separately but failure of sustained low-error convergence when combined at constant learning rate. They also report a promising cosine-derived schedule and argue that conventional optimization frameworks may struggle to explain these schedules.
record.recipe_differences: Studies exponential learning-rate schedules and their equivalence to conventional schedules with weight decay and momentum; includes a toy BN/weight-decay interaction analysis. This is not a direct test of the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: For the toy model, combining BN and weight decay changes convergence relative to either alone. For the PreResNet32 schedule comparison, instant learning-rate decay matters when the growth rate is very small; the cosine-hybrid result is reported only on CIFAR10.

fits_no_version.finding: In the Gaussian last-layer classification model, BN alone permits convergence and weight decay alone permits arbitrarily small error as batch size increases; their combination produces recurrent departures from a low-error region at constant learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN and weight decay can jointly prevent sustained low population classification error in a toy model even when either component alone permits convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: For scale-invariant objectives, exponential learning-rate schedules without weight decay can reproduce conventional training trajectories with weight decay and momentum. PreResNet32/CIFAR-10 experiments show similar performance, benefits from phase-transition learning-rate drops, and better test accuracy for a cosine-derived schedule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization-induced scale invariance permits schedule transformations that preserve network-function trajectories; particular schedule choices can affect test accuracy.

record.problems: The schedule experiments use PreResNet32 on CIFAR10 only, and the text gives no numeric training-error outcomes or uncertainty for those experiments. The toy theorem is a specific last-layer Gaussian binary-classification setting and does not establish results for benchmark CNN training.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numerical results were omitted. Results cited from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero CNN training classification error on CIFAR-10/100; random or corrupted labels; effects of size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious minima and their dependence on matched widths or extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation in plain networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and deep-network training with special initialization or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, training speed, and trainable depth.
Initial stability thresholds, transient loss increases with curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to those thresholds.
Accuracy gain speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BN, and Fixup's comparative speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The toy nonconvergence theorem does not challenge V1's benchmark CNN claim or V6's comparative speed claim. Neither nominal learning-rate growth nor the discussion of smoothness establishes V5's specified stability-threshold dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 training error under random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, initialization, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima, student versus teacher width, and outcomes as width grows.
Plain versus residual networks' depth-related training error, and Fixup or other methods for training deep networks without normalization.
Activation-matched or orthogonal initialization, gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Training above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence boundaries.
BN versus no-BN accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance on the listed image datasets; Fixup comparisons.

conditions.value: binary classification; label is sign of first coordinate
standard Gaussian inputs; batch size assumed very large

rows.value: can achieve O(√(ηλ/B)) test error; training error outcome not separately quantified
rows.locator: Section 3, Case 1: WD alone; Appendix A.6
rows.note: The text describes convergence toward the regularized objective's global minimum and gives an error bound for test error, not a numerical training-error result.
rows.check: The reported bound concerns population classification error under Gaussian inputs, not measured finite-sample training error. This toy last-layer model is outside V1's CNN setting.

rows.subject: SGD with BN alone (toy last-layer model)
rows.operation_detail: SGD with constant learning rate and BN after the linear layer, with BN scale and bias fixed

conditions.value: binary classification; label is sign of first coordinate
standard Gaussian inputs; batch size assumed very large

rows.value: SGD can find the unique global minimum; no numeric training-error value stated
rows.uncertainty: constant probability statements for gradient behavior; no numeric uncertainty for final error
rows.note: The authors state convergence to the unique global minimum, but do not state a measured final classification error value.
rows.check: Qualitative convergence in a normalized toy linear model does not measure BN's comparative speed or learning-rate tolerance. No numerical training-error outcome is reported.

rows.subject: SGD with BN and weight decay (toy last-layer model)
rows.operation_detail: SGD with constant learning rate and weight decay, without momentum, with BN after the linear layer

conditions.value: binary classification; label is sign of first coordinate
standard Gaussian inputs; batch size assumed very large
every stated consecutive window after any starting iteration T0

rows.measure: training classification error; theorem bounds how often it exceeds πε
rows.baseline: BN alone and weight decay alone discussed as convergent cases
rows.value: training error is larger than πε at least once during a window of 2(ηλ−2ε²)⁻¹ ln(64||wT0||² ε B/(η√(m−2))) + 9 ln(1/δ) consecutive iterations, with probability 1−δ
rows.uncertainty: probability 1−δ; theorem's ε, η, λ, B, m, δ are parameters
rows.note: The theorem states repeated failure to remain below the specified training-error threshold when BN and weight decay are combined in this toy setup.
rows.check: The nonconvergence result is outside all versions, so observed is not a state relative to a linked version. The extracted window incorrectly substitutes B for sqrt(B). The source also inconsistently relates its error threshold to angle: the main theorem prints πε, while error = angle/π and the appendix uses angle ε. Preserve this source inconsistency rather than treating the threshold as unambiguous. The error is defined over the Gaussian population.

rows.subject: PreResNet32
rows.operation_detail: Compared the TEXP exponential learning-rate schedule with the schedule-equivalent Step Decay trajectory
rows.measure: trajectory and performance (the text does not report training classification error numerically)
rows.baseline: Step Decay schedule with weight decay
rows.value: TEXP and Step Decay have similar trajectories and performances, as predicted by the equivalence theorem
rows.note: The reported comparison concerns trajectory and performance, with no explicit training-error value; the figure caption also describes the first-convolution weight norm growing exponentially.
rows.check: This is the study's schedule-equivalence comparison, not evidence of near-zero training error or a BN versus no-BN comparison. Exponentially growing nominal learning rates do not establish operation above an initial stability threshold.
